piezas.titular: From the character who warped within eight seconds to models that keep them the same from scene to scene
piezas.entradilla: In November 2025, animating a character with Veo 3 meant cutting the clip before it stopped looking like itself. Today Google promises to keep it consistent from scene to scene.
cuerpo: On 8 November 2025, in EduMedia-IAG, several teachers who were producing videos shared the same frustration: in Veo 3 Fast, the character prepared as a reference image warped during the eight seconds of the clip, and in the next shot barely resembled itself. The fixes were makeshift: a storyboard of images drawn up beforehand, the exact description of the character repeated in every prompt, a saved frame to start the next scene, or a reminder that the dialogue had to fit into eight seconds. Some had been through fourteen attempts.

[Veo 3.1](https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/products/veo-updates-flow/), unveiled on 15 October 2025, already allowed scenes to be extended in Flow, but in the group the drift continued. On 19 May 2026, Google brought [Gemini Omni](https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/models-and-research/google-labs/flow-updates/) to Flow, which, according to its announcement, preserves the character's identity and voice in every scene and lets users edit the video through conversation. The [Gemini Omni page](https://gemini.google/overview/video-generation/) says it will replace Veo in the Gemini app.

On 5 November 2026 came [Omni 1.2 Flash, which the paper reported on 6 November](pieza:2026-11-05/gemini-omni-1-2-flash): clips of up to 15 seconds and, according to Google, fewer distortions between the first and the last frame. What used to take hours, keeping the character the same, is now, on paper, the model's job.

piezas.ilustracion_alt: Diptych split by a vertical line. On the left, “Nov. 2025”: an “8 s” bar with one character at the start and, after the cut, another drawn warped and in dashes. On the right, “Today”: a longer “15 s” bar with the same character repeated three times, identical, in blue.
repaso: Quitada la frase «Iterar sigue gastando créditos»: no figura en ninguna fuente de hoy (venía del resumen de 2025) y la pieza pasaba de 250 palabras (251).
«Había quien lo intentaba catorce veces» → «Había quien llevaba catorce intentos», más fiel al mensaje original.
piezas.comprobado: Mensaje t.me/EduMediaIAG/5972 abierto: es el de jmga sobre Veo 3 Fast, personaje desfigurado en 8 s y plano siguiente inconsistente. Entrada del 8-nov-2025 (#5961-#6015): guion gráfico, descripción repetida, fotograma guardado, diálogo en 8 s, 14 intentos (#6006), sin nombres en el texto. Reabiertas las cuatro fuentes: blog de Veo 3.1 (15-oct-2025, Extend en Flow); blog de Flow (19-may-2026, Omni Flash en Flow, «identity and voice are preserved across every scene», iteración conversacional); gemini.google/overview/video-generation («Gemini Omni sustituirá a Veo en la aplicación Gemini»); blog de Omni 1.2 Flash (5-nov-2026, hasta 15 s, menos deriva y deformaciones del primer al último fotograma, afirmaciones de Google). Enlace pieza:2026-11-05/gemini-omni-1-2-flash presente en publicado.txt, publicado el 6-nov-2026 y sobre el mismo tema. Medida: 245 palabras con la entradilla.
